transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Rafael Torres (Redwood CSM), Priya Singh (Nimbus Head of ML), Owen Martinez (Platform Eng), Lydia Park (Procurement), Samir Halim (Security)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion check-in. Customer looking to extend contract for another 12 months, add Dedicated capacity (+20%), and onboard EU region for latency/residency. Discussed pricing, SLA, private/VPC constraints, and security docs. Agreed on benchmark run and updated quote.

Topics: renewal timeline; capacity sizing; EU region onboarding; private deployment vs hosted routing; SLA and audit docs; procurement next steps

Action items (captured verbally and repeated at end): see structured action_items field.

Transcript: 
00:00 Maya: okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 minutes ish, um kickoff — Maya from Redwood, i have Jordan and Rafael with me.
00:06 Priya: hey thanks, Priya here. We wanted to make sure we tie up the renewal and get the EU region live before Q2.
00:11 Owen: yeah, latency from EU customers is still in the 220 to 300 millisecond tail for us, so that's driving some churn in our field agents.
00:18 Jordan: got it. quick clarifying q, current Dedicated pool is what size again? i have notes that we're on a 40-GPU reserved pool but usage peaks are hitting about 85% during daytime windows?
00:27 Priya: yep that's right — we provisioned 40, peaks around 34 to 36 concurrent lanes, but token throughput spikes with batch jobs and overnight jobs.
00:35 Maya: so today's ask is 1) renew the contract for 12 months, 2) add EU region with parity to NA, and 3) bump dedicated by 20% — i think that's what we heard?
00:43 Priya: exactly. also procurement wants any SLA tweaks and the security team wants the SOC2 addendum and KMS details.
00:50 Samir: yeah on security, two quick things: we need to confirm customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS options), audit log retention windows, and proof of encryption in transit and at rest. Also any private deployment offering — we may need a VPC peering option for the EU region.
01:05 Maya: 100%. We have private deployment (we call it Redwood Private) and Dedicated is separate; sorry sometimes the product names get munged in notes, um; we can do customer KMS via bring-your-own-key, and audit logs are configurable to 12+ months depending on plan.
01:17 Priya: do you have an SLA example for throughput and tail latency? our SLO is 95th < 120ms for interactive flows.
01:25 Jordan: depending on model and sequence length we can get to low 100s in EU with a local region; the Dedicated pool plus caching will help. i want to caveat that batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency if not tuned — we'll surface the tradeoffs in the benchmark.
01:38 Owen: curious, you mentioned KV cache earlier in the email — is that prefix caching or like full session cache? we've seen some folks call it KV cash in logs :), sorry bad joke.
01:45 Jordan: ha, KV cache — yes it's prefix/KV cache, saves about 20-35% token cost on our workloads typically but depends on prompt patterns.
01:51 Lydia: on procurement rhythm, we need an updated quote that separates NA and EU line items, and a renewal amendment we can attach to the PO.
01:59 Maya: we can do line-itemized pricing; we'll include committed usage tiers for Dedicated and optional burst capacity.
02:06 Samir: another security ask — do you offer private control plane for EU? we can't send certain telemetry outside region until legal signs off.
02:14 Rafael: we have a Private deployment option that can be hosted in a customer VPC or on-prem; for region residency we can restrict control plane endpoints to the EU region but will need to scope network peering and runbook changes. we'll document the network flows.
02:25 Priya: timeline wise how long to get EU region live if we sign this month?
02:29 Jordan: rough estimate: 4-6 weeks for Dedicated pools and region provisioning, shorter if we reuse existing infra templates; if Private deployment with customer networking it's more like 6-10 weeks depending on procurement and security signoffs.
02:40 Priya: that's doable but we need to start the bench asap.
02:44 Maya: agreed. Jordan will coordinate the benchmark — typical run is 2 hours of steady-state plus spike tests. we'll run both small and large sequence workloads.
02:53 Jordan: for the benchmark we'll need a sample workload, token counts, and a list of models you plan to serve — also any special quantization or custom weights.
03:00 Priya: sending sample prompts and token distribution by EOD today.
03:04 Owen: also note we have an internal model fork (V2-light) that we've been using; curious whether Redwood has verified perf for forked weights or we should treat it as a custom onboarding.
03:12 Jordan: if it's a fork we treat like a custom model; performance can vary — we'll run perf estimates and, where possible, use the same kernel paths. sometimes names in our system get munged — so we may call it Redwood-verified, but if it's custom it needs full onboarding.
03:24 Lydia: any impact to pricing if we add EU? we want predictable unit economics.
03:28 Maya: we'll show committed discounts for multi-region + committed compute. the quote will compare hosted usage rates vs Dedicated unit costs. adding EU Dedicated will be additive but the committed tier stepdown applies.
03:38 Samir: procurement: we have a supplier approval board next week, can you provide SOC2, encryption docs, and a standard addendum by Friday?
03:45 Rafael: yes we'll share the security pack link in the chat — includes SOC2 summary, encryption-at-rest details, KMS options, and data processing addendum.
03:52 Maya: quick note, competitors were mentioned — you said you evaluated LambdaLabs and CloudAI Managed Endpoints — can you share specifics so we can address gaps?
04:01 Priya: LambdaLabs had cheaper headline price but poor EMEA infra; CloudAI had a nicer SSO/SSO flow but the throughput made costs unpredictable.
04:10 Jordan: good context — we'll make sure the benchmark highlights cost per 1k tokens alongside tail latency so you can compare.
04:18 Owen: question about burst capacity — we want to keep base Dedicated to cover 99th of normal traffic and burst for seasonal spikes. how's burst billing handled?
04:27 Maya: burst is billed at on-demand incremental rate; we can include burst caps and automated fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated saturated — that's part of the rollout policy.
04:36 Priya: can you put that fallback policy in writing? we need deterministic behavior for outage scenarios.
04:41 Rafael: yes, we'll include the automatic fallback policy, canary rollout steps, and rollback criteria in the onboarding doc.
04:48 Samir: small transcription note in my head — do you support customer-managed HSM or just KMS?
04:52 Jordan: both typically — HSM integrations via common vendors and cloud KMS are supported, we'll list specifics in the security pack.
04:59 Lydia: procurement would like a target signature date — our board wants the contract signed before Jan 31 to hit FY commitments.
05:06 Maya: we can aim for that. we'll get the amended proposal by 1/13, then procurement reviews, and target 1/28 signature — sounds okay?
05:14 Lydia: that would work if docs arrive on time.
05:18 Priya: one other nit: token accounting for embeddings vs generation needs to be clearly separated on invoice.
05:24 Maya: understood — we'll break out line items by endpoint type.
05:29 Owen: last tech quickie — any limits on KV cache size per session? we saw some folks hitting eviction in peak.
05:35 Jordan: eviction is LRU based and configurable per model group; we can increase capacity on Dedicated but it affects memory footprint, which we'll quantify in the benchmark.
05:44 Maya: ok let's recap next steps. Maya to send amended quote with NA/EU line items and committed tiers; Jordan to run benchmark next Tue and share results; Rafael to push security pack and onboarding playbook; Samir to provide compliance checklist; Procurement (Lydia) to review contract and propose PO timeline.
05:58 Priya: thanks all, good meeting. we'll wait for the quote and the benchmark invite.
06:03 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and slack. bye.

End of transcript. Shared links mentioned in call: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (security pack & SOC2), https://redwood.ai/pricing/nimbus-amendment (proposed commercial template placeholder), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nimbus-harness (benchmark harness sheet).
